although

conjunction
 OPAL WOPAL S
 
/ɔːlˈðəʊ/
 
/ɔːlˈðəʊ/
(US English, informal altho)
jump to other results
  1.  
     used for introducing a statement that makes the main statement in a sentence seem surprising synonym though
    • Although the sun was shining, it wasn't very warm.
    • Although small, the kitchen is well designed.
    Language Bank howeverhoweverWays of saying ‘but’
      • Politicians have promised to reduce air pollution. So far, however, little has been achieved.
      • Despite clear evidence from studies of air pollution, no new measures have been introduced.
      • Politicians have promised to reduce air pollution. In spite of this/Despite this, little has been achieved so far.
      • Although politicians have promised to reduce air pollution, little has been achieved so far.
      • Some politicians claim that the new policy on air pollution has been a success. In fact, it has been a total disaster.
      • Government campaigns have had a measure of success, but the fact remains that significant numbers of early deaths are still caused by air pollution.
  2.  
     used to mean ‘but’ or ‘however’ when you are commenting on a statement
    • I felt he was wrong, although I didn't say so at the time.
    3. Word OriginMiddle English: from the adverb all + though.
